original_card.question: Can one uncovered interface implication be formalized with exact caller and certificate bindings?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Inventory the gate-operand parity lemma (#3807) and certified endpoint arithmetic (#3857). Neither is a full multiplication proof. For #4100, audit the compact-switch statement and its hypotheses before formalizing it.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

existing_checks.remaining: Exact theorem-to-caller binding and genuinely uncovered interface lemmas.
Uniform algorithmic implications, not another endpoint digit.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Evaluate r(2/B+beta) against C p 2^{-G} at r=r_max on the one admitted layout p=2, ell=2, L=65536, and name the constant that replaces 1/6400 there.
scope_change_reason: PR #4913 showed that this layout has L > p, so the production factor 1/6400 does not transfer. The successive sixteenth walks are closed. This package evaluates that one inequality. It does not retune the production plan, does not rerun the descriptor census, and does not claim a new kappa.
bottleneck_link: The sharp-density line uses C=1/6400 only under L <= p. On this layout the exact ratio is strictly between 2 and 3, so the smallest integer constant is 3. The selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop after this one layout at r=r_max, for the sharp window and the published window term. Do not scan other layouts or replay the 104864-plan census.
author: James Reed

open_questions.question: For every layout the #4174 constructor accepts, is C = 3 r_max / p sufficient for r(2/B+beta) <= C p 2^{-G} at r = r_max?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The constant 3 is proved here only for p=2 and ell=2. A uniform factor would say when 1/6400 still applies and when it must grow.
open_questions.first_step: Show that every accepted layout has G >= 256, so 2 + 2^{1-62G} < 3.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package checks only the one longer layout.
